GENETIC LABORATORY REPORT

Patient Information:
Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sex: Female
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Department: Pediatric Genetics
Hospital: [redacted location]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Infant referred for genetic evaluation
Clinical Indication: Suspected Down Syndrome (T21)

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Trisomy Screening Panel

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on genomic DNA extracted from whole blood to assess copy number of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Multiple short tandem repeat (STR) markers were amplified for each chromosome:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437

Fluorescent PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Peak area ratios were calculated to determine chromosome copy number.

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers

Result Summary: rsa(13,18,21)×2

INTERPRETATION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormalities detected. This result excludes non-mosaic trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this patient.

LIMITATIONS
- This test is designed to detect complete trisomies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Segmental imbalances, balanced rearrangements, and other chromosomal abnormalities are not detected by this method
- Abnormalities of other chromosomes are not assessed

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
Normal chromosomal complement for tested chromosomes. No evidence of trisomy conditions including Down syndrome.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full chromosome analysis to follow this preliminary report. If clinical suspicion remains high, comprehensive chromosomal microarray or karyotype analysis is recommended to evaluate for other chromosomal abnormalities not detected by this targeted screening test.

Test performed by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Laboratory Director
Report Date: [redacted date]

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Clinical Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
